title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 367
paragraphs: This Psammetichos had previously been a fugitive from the Ethiopian Sabacos, who had killed his father Necos; from him, I say, he had been a fugitive in Syria. When the Ethiopian departed as a result of the vision in the dream, the Egyptians of the district of Saïs brought him back to his own country. Afterwards, when he was king, it was his fate to be a fugitive a second time on account of the helmet, being driven by the eleven kings into the marshland. Holding that he had been gravely wronged by them, he considered how he might take vengeance on those who had driven him out. When he sent to the oracle of Leto in the city of Buto, where the Egyptians have their most truthful oracle, he was given the reply that vengeance would come when men of bronze appeared from the sea. He was strongly inclined not to believe that bronze men would come to help him; but not long afterwards, certain Ionians and Carians who had sailed out for plunder were forced to come ashore in Egypt, and having landed and being clad in bronze armor, one of the Egyptians, never having seen men in bronze armor before, came to the marshland and brought word to Psammetichos that bronze men had come from the sea and were plundering the plain. He, perceiving that the saying of the oracle was coming to pass, dealt in a friendly manner with the Ionians and Carians, and with large promises persuaded them to take his side. Then, having persuaded them, with the help of the Egyptians who favored his cause and of these foreign mercenaries, he overthrew the kings.
